Q: Do not stop loop if creation fails when creating objects in loop A:

Your code looks fine to me, just finish setting up the logger:

import logging
import os


# LOGLEVEL = os.environ.get('LOGLEVEL', 'WARNING').upper() # https://powerfulpython.com/blog/nifty-python-logging-trick/
# logging.basicConfig(level=os.environ.get("LOGLEVEL"))    # https://powerfulpython.com/blog/nifty-python-logging-trick/

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

root_log = logging.getLogger("my-logger")
log = logging.getLogger("my-logger")
log.info("...starting log !!!")

class DivisionCreationError(Exception):
    pass

class Division(object):
    def __init__(self, a, b):
        self.a = a
        self.b = b
    
        try:
            self.a / self.b
            log.info('data : '+str(self.a)+'/'+str(self.b))
        except ZeroDivisionError:
            log.info('data : '+str(self.a)+'/'+str(self.b))
            log.warning('Not possible')
            raise DivisionCreationError
        else:
            self.result = self.a / self.b
        
    def get_result(self):
        log.info('result : '+str(self.result))
        return self.result
        
if __name__ == '__main__':
    
    numbers = [(1,2), (1,0), (1,3)]
    
    for i in numbers:
        print(i)
        try:
            created_object = Division(i[0], i[1])
        except DivisionCreationError:
            pass
        else:
            print('--> ',created_object.get_result())

Q: Return row numbers in Excel VBA - SQL A:

Calculate Item number with subquery

    strSQL = "SELECT [ID], Sum([QTY]) As myQTY,  Round(myTOTAL/myQTY,2) As myPRICE, Sum([TOTAL]) As myTOTAL " & _
            " ,(SELECT count(*) " & _
            "   FROM (SELECT [ID] FROM [ASDRT$]  UNION  SELECT [ID] FROM [FSR$])t2" & _
            "   WHERE t2.[ID]< t.[ID]" & _
            "   )+1 As Item " & _
            "FROM " & _
             " ( " & _
             "   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [ASDRT$] " & _
             "   UNION ALL " & _
             "   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [FSR$] " & _
             " )t " & _
             "WHERE [ID]<>'' " & _
             "GROUP BY [ID]" & _
             "ORDER BY [ID]"

Item number calculation require "order" definition. In this example items ordered by Id. I added the order (ORDER BY) to the query.

(SELECT count(*) 
 FROM (SELECT Id FROM [ASDRT$] union SELECT Id FROM [FSR$]) t2
 WHERE t2.id< t.Id
 )+1 As Item

In words: count the number of IDs that are less than the current one.

Similar to

   SELECT dense_rank()over(order by Id) as Item
   FROM (SELECT Id FROM [ASDRT$] UNION SELECT Id FROM [FSR$]) t2

"UNION" is used in subquery, so Id's is unique and row_number() and dense_rank() will get same values.

Update1. This expression

(SELECT count(*) 
 FROM (SELECT [ID] FROM [ASDRT$]  UNION  SELECT [ID] FROM [FSR$])t2
 WHERE t2.[ID]< t.[ID]
)+1 As Item

is a regular calculated column that can be placed anywhere in the select list.

SELECT 
   (SELECT count(*)
    FROM (SELECT [ID] FROM [ASDRT$]  UNION  SELECT [ID] FROM [FSR$])t2
    WHERE t2.[ID]< t.[ID])+1 As Item,
   [ID], Sum([QTY]) As myQTY,  Round(myTOTAL/myQTY,2) As myPRICE, 
   Sum([TOTAL]) As myTOTAL
FROM (
   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [ASDRT$]
   UNION ALL
   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [FSR$]
   )t
WHERE [ID]<>''
GROUP BY [ID]
ORDER BY [ID]

Q: Openapi generator use validation annotation on getter not on field A:

What issue you encountered I cannot tell based on this, however I would like to point out that validation should still work whether it's defined on the field or the accessor. According to the Jakarta validation spec - Field and property validation:

When using field access strategy, the Jakarta Validation provider accesses the instance variable directly. When using the property access strategy, the Jakarta Validation provider accesses the state via the property accessor method.

Q: How to change argv[0] value in shell / bash script? A:

You can also use the env command to set argv0. Unfortunately none of these methods work with shell scripts which have a shebang at the top of the file.

$ env --argv0=meow sh -c "echo argv0 is \$0"
argv0 is meow

Q: How to pass & correctly escape HTTP headers/arguments to curl in a bash script? A:

I suppose the issue is with the last line where you actually execute the curl command. See

/usr/local/bin/curl "${HDR[@]/#/-H }" "@"
#                                     ^^^ this is an incorrect token, should have been "$@"

The actual positional arguments list in bash is "$@" which should have been used in your command as

/usr/local/bin/curl "${HDR[@]/#/-H }" "$@"
